title: One working source_id end to end: committed-input test credit in real repositories with submodules (TermAl and Engram)
outcome: Real Questly and PhoenixCodeNav checkouts, clean with every submodule initialized at its pin, earn a registered committed-input verification that Engram accepts at exactly that commit, through the ordinary launcher route, as one joint TermAl and Engram result. Reporting-only observations never count. Parts: TermAl w-c07c410dac75 (capture and host admission) and Engram w-7828ac63767b (reader).
acceptance: On the installed builds of both projects, after the joint restart, an agent in the real Questly and PhoenixCodeNav checkouts, on Linux (DL560) and on Windows, runs the repository's committed declared test command as the first tool activity of a fresh turn. TermAl captures the full source_id from `engram source` before dispatch (S0) and after the run. The two are equal, local changes are allowed, and a clean checkout is not required. TermAl validates the real result artifact and sends a registered verification, which Engram stores and accepts on the bound work for done, with evaluations off. No reporting-only observation counts.

A source change between S0 and the after capture gets no credit, with a named reason: an edited tracked file, a new non-ignored untracked file, or a changed submodule HEAD. So does an unavailable source_id (timeout, size bound or filters). This holds on Linux and on Windows. The documented option-B limits are accepted: a change fully reverted in between, edits that git status does not report, and changes to ignored files.
There is no exclusion list or profile; Git-ignored output stays outside the source_id. No stored evaluation, verification or seal is changed, and repositories without submodules work the same way.
Each part lands under its own project's standing rule. Criterion 1 needs the installed builds, so it is verified only after install and restart, and this item completes only then.
